commands.short: Run a security scan

flags.name: allow-private-targets
flags.usage: Allow the scanner to connect to private/loopback/link-local addresses and the cloud metadata IP (disables the SSRF egress guard). Auto-enabled when --url already resolves to a private/loopback host.

flags.name: allow-repo-local-plugins
flags.usage: Opt in to running repo-local plugins under <scan-dir>/.fendix/plugins/ (UNSAFE on untrusted PRs; ~/.fendix/plugins/ is always trusted)

flags.name: auth
flags.usage: Auth header value, e.g. "Bearer token123"

flags.name: auth-header
flags.usage: Custom auth header name; with apikey-query this names the query parameter (pass api_key for the conventional name)

flags.name: auth-type
flags.usage: Auth type: bearer, apikey, apikey-query, basic, cookie (default: auto-detect)

flags.name: auth-user2
flags.usage: Second user auth for IDOR checks, e.g. "Bearer token-user2"

flags.name: baseline
flags.usage: Path to a baseline (from --save-baseline) or JSON report; only occurrences not proven present in it are reported

flags.name: block-on-inapplicable
flags.usage: Gate the build on a vulnerable dependency even when Fendix found no import of the advisory's affected component. Default false: such a finding is reported in full and held at WARN, because the vulnerable code path is not applicable to this project on the available evidence. Set this when policy is "no vulnerable version ships, applicable or not" — e.g. where the SBOM is what gets audited rather than the call graph.

flags.name: checks
flags.usage: Override checks when the Python whitebox engine runs (default: auth,injection,deps). --code auto-enables that phase unless --python-engine=false is explicit; the native Go scanners run independently.

flags.name: code
flags.usage: Path to source code directory (white-box scanning)

flags.name: config
flags.usage: Path to .fendix.yaml policy file (default: auto-detect .fendix.yaml in cwd)

flags.name: crawl-depth
flags.usage: Recursive HTML link crawl depth (0 disables; 1 = home-page links only)

flags.name: debug-bundle
flags.usage: Write a redacted diagnostic tarball to this path at scan end (intended for bug reports)

flags.name: deescalate-tests
flags.usage: Report findings in test/fixture code as INFO instead of WARN (evidence is preserved, never suppressed). A finding at or above --fail-on can still block when independent corroboration supports it; an unsupported test-code match is held at WARN. Pass --deescalate-tests=false to treat test-code findings like production ones.

flags.name: delay
flags.usage: Milliseconds between HTTP requests

flags.name: diff
flags.usage: Diff-aware scan: only scan files changed vs a git ref (bare --diff = vs HEAD, --diff=origin/main = vs that ref). Whitebox scanners are scoped to the changed files; dep-CVE scanners run only when a manifest changed.

flags.name: enable-active
flags.usage: Enable active injection probes (default: false)

flags.name: enforce-confidence
flags.usage: Only BLOCK a finding at or above --fail-on when the confidence band supports it AND something corroborates the claim: LOW band warns; a finding with no corroborating signal at all warns; MEDIUM band blocks only with an INDEPENDENT signal (cross-engine agreement, confirmed route, reachable taint path, proven path, payload-validated probe, cross-tool corroboration, contradicted authentication requirement); self-evident signals (direct response read, deterministic detection in production source, imported high-precision rule) gate at HIGH. Evidence is never suppressed. Pass --enforce-confidence=false to restore the legacy severity-only gate — findings that block only because of that relaxation are marked policy_override in the report.

flags.name: fail-on
flags.usage: Exit 1 if a finding at this severity reaches BLOCK: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW (confidence gating applies — see --enforce-confidence)

flags.name: fail-on-coverage-gap
flags.usage: Exit 2 when an analyzer this run was configured to execute was unavailable or failed (metadata.coverage.configured_complete=false). Disabled, not-applicable and unsupported analyzers never trip it.

flags.name: fail-on-scanner-error
flags.usage: Exit non-zero (2) if any recorded analyzer — any entry in metadata.scanner_status, which is the full registry (dast, spec, active-probes, secrets, textscan, semgrep, govulncheck, pip, npm, plugins, the python-engine and its checks) — ran and errored. CI-friendly: turns a silent coverage gap into a build failure. Skipped entries never count.

flags.name: fast
flags.usage: Skip semgrep and the native dependency scanners. Known limitation: --fast does not disable the Python engine auto-enabled by --code; add --python-engine=false when a native-only pre-commit scan is required.

flags.name: format
flags.usage: Output format: json, html, sarif, pdf

flags.name: ignore
flags.usage: Path to .fendix-ignore file

flags.name: import
flags.usage: Merge findings from another scanner's SARIF 2.1.0 file into this scan (repeatable). Imported findings go through the standard pipeline; a native fendix finding at the same weakness+location becomes strong cross-tool corroboration. See also the standalone 'fendix import' command.

flags.name: lang
flags.usage: HTML report language: en (default), ar (Arabic, RTL). Other formats stay English.

flags.name: managed-context
flags.usage: Path to the runner-supplied managed-CI context (managed-scan-context/v1 plus evidence_submission_id).

flags.name: managed-evidence
flags.usage: Write the managed-CI submission document (contract managed-ci/v2) to this path. Requires --managed-context.

flags.name: max-duration
flags.usage: Soft-cap on total scan wall-clock time, e.g. 5m (0 = no cap)

flags.name: max-endpoints
flags.usage: Cap total discovered endpoints (0 = no cap)

flags.name: max-probes-per-endpoint
flags.usage: Max active probes per endpoint (only effective with --enable-active)

flags.name: max-requests
flags.usage: Soft-cap on total HTTP requests across all checks (0 = no cap)

flags.name: no-native-deps
flags.usage: Disable the in-process Go dep-CVE scanner (TASK-119). Defer to the Python deps.py path instead.

flags.name: no-plugins
flags.usage: Disable out-of-tree plugin discovery in .fendix/plugins/ + ~/.fendix/plugins/

flags.name: offline
flags.usage: Use the local offline-db snapshot for native pip/npm CVEs and skip native govulncheck (create the snapshot with 'fendix db update'). Known limitation: the Python deps check auto-enabled by --code does not receive this flag and may run networked tools; for a hermetic scan add --checks auth,injection or --python-engine=false.

flags.name: offline-db
flags.usage: Path to the offline-db snapshot (default: ~/.fendix/offline-db.json). Only effective with --offline.

flags.name: output
flags.usage: Output file path (default: stdout)

flags.name: profile
flags.usage: Auth profile name from ~/.fendix/profiles/<name>.yaml

flags.name: python-engine
flags.usage: Spawn the Python whitebox engine for auth/injection/deps checks (TASK-118). --code enables it automatically unless --python-engine=false is explicit. Standalone binaries do not bundle the engine; provide a local python/ tree or FENDIX_ENGINE (the official container supplies one).

flags.name: require-analyzers
flags.usage: Comma-separated analyzer names that must be delivered (recorded ok or not_applicable) for exit 0; anything else exits 2. Stricter than --fail-on-coverage-gap: a required analyzer disabled by another flag is a contradiction and exits 2. Names: dast, spec, active-probes, secrets, textscan, semgrep, govulncheck, pip, npm, python-engine, python-engine/auth, python-engine/injection, python-engine/deps, plugins

flags.name: respect-robots
flags.usage: Treat robots.txt Disallow as a hard restriction (default: queue as discovery hints)

flags.name: save-baseline
flags.usage: Save current findings, with every occurrence identity, to this path (baseline format v2)

flags.name: spec
flags.usage: Path or HTTP(S) URL to an OpenAPI/Swagger YAML or JSON spec

flags.name: staged
flags.usage: Diff-aware scan over staged changes only (git diff --cached). Implies --diff. This is what the pre-commit hook runs.

flags.name: timeout
flags.usage: HTTP timeout in seconds

flags.name: url
flags.usage: Target API base URL (black-box scanning)

flags.name: use-pip-audit
flags.usage: Shell out to the pip-audit binary for Python dep-CVE scanning instead of the native OSV.dev client. Falls back to OSV.dev with a warning if pip-audit is not on PATH.

flags.name: verbose
flags.usage: Print all requests and raw findings

flags.name: wordlist
flags.usage: Path to brute-force wordlist (one path per line); overrides built-in CommonPaths

flags.name: workers
flags.usage: Concurrent HTTP workers
